title: GRE & Quants
notes: VERBAL STRATEGY: Read the entire passage/sentence BEFORE looking at answer choices
TEXT COMPLETION: Look for signal words (although, moreover, however, but) to understand sentence logic
TEXT COMPLETION: Predict your own word for the blank, then find similar choices
SENTENCE EQUIVALENCE: Two correct words must make sentences with THE SAME MEANING, not just be synonyms
READING COMP: Focus on main idea, author's tone, and passage structure
READING COMP: Eliminate choices that are only partially true or go beyond passage scope
READING COMP: All answers must be based ONLY on information in the passage
VOCAB: GRE tests secondary/less common meanings of familiar words in context
VOCAB: Learn word roots (ben-=good, mal-=bad, dict-=say, anthrop-=human, ambi-=both)
QUANT: Figures are NOT drawn to scale - rely on given information only
QUANT: Coordinate graphs, number lines, and data charts ARE drawn to scale
QUANT: All numbers are real numbers unless stated otherwise
QUANT: Round only the final answer to avoid cumulative rounding errors
QUANT COMPARISON: Plug in numbers (0, 1, -1, fractions) to test relationships
QUANT COMPARISON: If relationship changes with different values, answer is always 'cannot be determined'
QUANT COMPARISON: Simplify by subtracting same quantity from both sides
QUANT: Use calculator for tedious arithmetic, but mental math is often faster
QUANT: Backsolve by plugging answer choices into the problem
QUANT: For 'select all that apply', evaluate each choice independently
GEOMETRY: Pythagorean theorem a²+b²=c² for right triangles
GEOMETRY: Circle area = πr², circumference = 2πr
GEOMETRY: Triangle area = ½×base×height
GEOMETRY: Rectangle area = length×width, perimeter = 2(l+w)
GEOMETRY: Volume of rectangular solid = length×width×height
GEOMETRY: Cylinder volume = πr²h, surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh
GEOMETRY: Sphere volume = (4/3)πr³, surface area = 4πr²
GEOMETRY: Sum of angles in triangle = 180°
GEOMETRY: Sum of angles in quadrilateral = 360°
GEOMETRY: Special right triangles: 30-60-90 (sides: x, x√3, 2x) and 45-45-90 (sides: x, x, x√2)
ALGEBRA: Solve equations by isolating variable
ALGEBRA: Factor quadratics: x²+bx+c = (x+m)(x+n) where m+n=b and m×n=c
ALGEBRA: FOIL method: (a+b)(c+d) = ac+ad+bc+bd
ALGEBRA: Difference of squares: a²-b² = (a+b)(a-b)
ALGEBRA: Exponent rules: x^a × x^b = x^(a+b), x^a / x^b = x^(a-b), (x^a)^b = x^(ab)
ALGEBRA: x^0 = 1 for any x≠0, x^(-a) = 1/x^a
ALGEBRA: Slope = (y₂-y₁)/(x₂-x₁), slope-intercept form: y=mx+b
ALGEBRA: Distance between points: d = √[(x₂-x₁)²+(y₂-y₁)²]
ARITHMETIC: Prime numbers are divisible only by 1 and themselves (2,3,5,7,11,13...)
ARITHMETIC: Even×Even=Even, Odd×Odd=Odd, Even×Odd=Even
ARITHMETIC: Even+Even=Even, Odd+Odd=Even, Even+Odd=Odd
ARITHMETIC: Percent change = (New-Old)/Old × 100%
ARITHMETIC: Fraction operations: a/b × c/d = ac/bd, a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c
ARITHMETIC: To compare fractions, cross-multiply: a/b vs c/d → compare ad vs bc
STATISTICS: Mean = sum of values / number of values
STATISTICS: Median = middle value when ordered (or average of two middle values)
STATISTICS: Mode = most frequently occurring value
STATISTICS: Range = maximum - minimum
STATISTICS: Standard deviation measures spread from the mean (larger = more spread)
PROBABILITY: P(event) = number of favorable outcomes / total number of outcomes
PROBABILITY: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events
PROBABILITY: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
PROBABILITY: P(not A) = 1 - P(A)
COMBINATIONS: nCr = n! / (r!(n-r)!) - order doesn't matter
PERMUTATIONS: nPr = n! / (n-r)! - order matters
DATA INTERPRETATION: Read titles, axes, legends, units, and scales carefully
DATA INTERPRETATION: Watch for units in thousands, millions, or percents
WRITING: Issue essay structure: Intro (thesis) → Body paragraphs (reasons+examples) → Conclusion
WRITING: Use specific examples from history, literature, current events, or hypotheticals
WRITING: Address counterarguments to show nuanced thinking
WRITING: Use transition words (furthermore, however, therefore, in contrast)
WRITING: Vary sentence structure and use precise vocabulary
WRITING: Spend ~5 min planning, ~20 min writing, ~5 min proofreading
COMMON TRAP: Don't assume 10% increase then 10% decrease returns to original (different bases)
COMMON TRAP: In Sentence Equivalence, two synonyms might not both fit the sentence context
COMMON TRAP: Answer choices may include true statements that don't answer the question

flashcards.front: Text Completion: What are signal words and why are they important?
flashcards.back: Words like 'although', 'however', 'moreover' that indicate contrast or continuation; they reveal the logic of the sentence

flashcards.front: Text Completion: What's the best approach to filling blanks?
flashcards.back: Predict your own word for each blank based on context, then find the choice that matches your prediction

flashcards.front: Sentence Equivalence: What must the two correct answers create?
flashcards.back: Sentences that mean THE SAME THING (not just two words that are synonyms)

flashcards.front: Reading Comprehension: What are you NOT allowed to use?
flashcards.back: Outside knowledge or specialized information - answers must be based ONLY on the passage

flashcards.front: Reading Comprehension: What should you focus on when reading?
flashcards.back: Main idea, author's tone/purpose, and how parts of the passage relate to each other

flashcards.front: Reading Comprehension: How do you eliminate wrong answers?
flashcards.back: Eliminate choices that are only partially true, go beyond the passage scope, or misrepresent what the passage says

flashcards.front: Quantitative Comparison: What should you do with variables?
flashcards.back: Plug in multiple values (0, 1, -1, 2, fractions) to test if relationship changes

flashcards.front: Quantitative Comparison: When is the answer 'cannot be determined'?
flashcards.back: When the relationship between quantities changes depending on which values you plug in

flashcards.front: Quantitative Comparison: How can you simplify?
flashcards.back: Add, subtract, multiply, or divide both sides by the same amount (watch out when multiplying/dividing by negatives)

flashcards.front: Are geometric figures drawn to scale on the GRE?
flashcards.back: NO - never trust visual appearance. Use given information and geometric principles only

flashcards.front: What IS drawn to scale on the GRE?
flashcards.back: Coordinate graphs, number lines, bar graphs, line graphs, pie charts, and other data displays
Do all calculations exactly, then round only the FINAL answer to avoid cumulative rounding errors

flashcards.front: When should you use the GRE calculator?
flashcards.back: For tedious arithmetic (long division, multiplying large numbers), but mental math/estimation is often faster
Plugging answer choices into the problem to see which one works - useful for word problems
